instruction: Explain the following AI research abstract in simple Hinglish.
input:
Title: Audio-Based Understanding of Audiobook Narration Appeal 
Abstract: Narration is central to the audiobook listening experience, shaping how listeners engage with and understand the content. This work explores how narration qualities shape an audiobook's appeal, noting that their effects can vary by genre, title, and audience. We extract vocal and acoustic features (e.g., tone, pace, loudness) from LibriVox using pre-trained audio models and analyse their relationship with consumption data (specifically, view-rate) and their interplay with genre and title. Despite limited consumption data, we find that acoustic information alone has a robust association with appeal, even after accounting for title effects. We further validate these findings using more nuanced proprietary engagement metrics. To our knowledge, this is the first systematic computational study linking narration qualities, genre, title, and audiobook consumption, highlighting the potential of data-driven insights to improve audiobook personalisation and narrator casting.
output:
Yeh research paper investigate karta hai ki audiobook narration ki quality listeners ko kitna appeal karti hai aur unki engagement ko kaise influence karti hai. Basically, ek narrator ki voice ke vocal aur acoustic features, jaise uski 'tone', bolne ki 'pace', aur 'loudness', yeh sab sunne wale ke experience ko bahut affect karte hain. Authors ne LibriVox dataset se yeh vocal aur acoustic features extract kiye, jiske liye unhone pre-trained audio models ka use kiya. Phir unhone in extracted features ka relationship 'consumption data' ke saath analyse kiya, specifically 'view-rate' ko as an indicator of appeal.

Unhone yeh bhi explore kiya ki narration qualities ka effect 'genre', 'title', aur 'audience' ke hisaab se kaise change hota hai. Despite limited consumption data, unka ek significant finding yeh hai ki 'acoustic information' ka 'appeal' ke saath ek robust association hai, even jab 'title effects' ko consider kiya jaata hai. Iska matlab hai ki narration ki underlying sound quality, content se alag bhi, listener engagement mein ek crucial role play karti hai. Iske findings ko authors ne 'proprietary engagement metrics' use karke further validate kiya. Yeh study important hai kyunki yeh pehli systematic computational research hai jo narration qualities, genre, title, aur audiobook consumption ko ek saath link karti hai. Isse future mein audiobook 'personalisation' aur 'narrator casting' decisions mein data-driven insights mil sakte hain.

instruction: Explain the following AI research abstract in simple Hinglish.
input:
Title: Interpretation-Oriented Cloud Removal via Observation-Anchored Residual Flow with Geo-Contextual Alignment 
Abstract: Cloud removal (CR) is essential for optical remote sensing, serving as a prerequisite for reliable downstream interpretation, such as semantic segmentation and change detection. However, existing CR approaches often prioritize visual realism while overlooking their impact on subsequent analytical tasks, leading to semantic drift and degraded downstream performance. To address this issue, we propose Geo-Anchored Cloud Removal (GACR), a unified framework that jointly ensures faithful reconstruction and robust interpretability. At its core, GACR incorporates Observation-Anchored Residual Flow (OAR-Flow), which reformulates CR as a physically grounded residual inversion process. By anchoring the generative trajectory to the cloudy observation rather than pure noise, OAR-Flow enables fast, stable, and faithful reconstruction. To further preserve semantic structures critical for downstream interpretation, GACR integrates Geo-Contextual Prior Alignment (GCPA) to constrain the reconstruction within a semantic manifold induced by a Vision Foundation Model (VFM). Consequently, GACR strictly maintains the spatial-semantic integrity of complex landscapes. Extensive experiments across six CR datasets and twelve downstream tasks demonstrate that GACR produces superior reconstruction quality while consistently improving downstream task accuracy. The code is available at https://github.com/wzy6055/GACR.
output:
Students, yeh paper Cloud Removal (CR) ke ek important problem ko address karta hai. Optical remote sensing mein, clouds ki wajah se images clear nahi hoti, aur unhe remove karna zaroori hai. Existing CR methods generally images ko visually realistic banane par focus karte hain, but is process mein original data ka semantic meaning change ho jaata hai. Isse 'semantic drift' kehte hain, aur iska impact downstream tasks jaise semantic segmentation ya change detection par negative hota hai, unki performance degrade ho jaati hai.

Is problem ko solve karne ke liye, yeh paper Geo-Anchored Cloud Removal (GACR) framework propose karta hai. GACR ka main aim hai ki reconstruction faithful ho aur saath hi robust interpretability bhi maintain ho. Iske core mein Observation-Anchored Residual Flow (OAR-Flow) hai. Yeh CR ko ek physically grounded residual inversion process ki tarah dekhta hai. Instead of generating from pure noise, OAR-Flow generative trajectory ko directly cloudy observation se anchor karta hai. Isse reconstruction fast, stable aur faithful banti hai.

Aur, downstream interpretation ke liye semantic structures ko preserve karne ke liye, GACR mein Geo-Contextual Prior Alignment (GCPA) bhi integrate kiya gaya hai. GCPA reconstruction ko ek semantic manifold ke andar constrain karta hai, jo ek Vision Foundation Model (VFM) se induced hota hai. Isse complex landscapes ki spatial-semantic integrity maintain rehti hai. Overall, GACR superior reconstruction quality deta hai aur downstream tasks mein accuracy ko consistently improve karta hai, jaisa ki experiments mein dikhaya gaya hai.

instruction: Explain the following AI research abstract in simple Hinglish.
input:
Title: TestEvo-Bench: An Executable and Live Benchmark for Test and Code Co-Evolution 
Abstract: Software tests and code evolve together: a code change should be followed by new or updated tests that record the new software behavior. Yet existing test generation and update benchmarks often isolate the test from the code change, and rely on static metadata that does not verify whether a test is executable or semantically tied to the code change. This makes it difficult to evaluate whether a test automation agent understands how a code change should propagate into the test suite.   We introduce TestEvo-Bench, a benchmark of test and code co-evolution tasks mined from software repositories, with two tracks: in test generation, the agent shall write new tests to capture the new software behavior; in test update, the agent shall adapt failing existing tests to the changed software behavior. Each task is anchored to a real commit history and packaged with environment configuration to support execution-grounded metrics such as pass rate, coverage, and mutation score. TestEvo-Bench is also a live benchmark: each task records the timestamp of the test and code changes, and new tasks are periodically mined by our automated pipeline, so evaluation can be restricted to tasks postdating a model's training cutoff to reduce data leakage risk. The current snapshot contains 746 test generation and 509 test update tasks, curated from 59,950 candidate co-evolution records across 152 open-source Java projects. We experiment with four state-of-the-art agents that combine strong harnesses (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and SWE-Agent) with strong foundation models (Claude Opus 4.7 and Gemini 3.1 Pro). Results show that they achieve up to 77.5% success rate on test generation and 74.6% on test update. However, success rate is materially lower on the most recent benchmark tasks and drops significantly under limited per-task cost.
output:

instruction: Explain the following AI research abstract in simple Hinglish.
input:
Title: Human Capital, Not Model Benchmarks, Predicts Hybrid Intelligence in Forecasting 
Abstract: Whether pairing people with AI helps or hurts is usually reported as a single average effect. Using a real-money prediction market (Polymarket) as an objective, externally resolved benchmark, this pilot shows that the value of human-AI collaboration depends on a specific, measurable form of human capital. Analyzed at the level of the individual forecaster, hybrid performance is trimodal: most people either deferred to the model (matching it) or used it to rubber-stamp a prior guess (performing worse than the model alone), while a minority engaged in genuine complementary reasoning and reached accuracy matching or even exceeding (i.e., lower error than) the market itself. Collaborative traits (perspective-taking, intellectual humility, and curiosity) rather than raw cognitive ability or model benchmarks, distinguished who reached that mode. The results are preliminary but statistically robust, and motivate a pre-registered replication now in preparation.
output:
Yeh paper explore karta hai ki jab hum humans ko AI ke saath pair karte hain forecasting ke liye, toh uska actual outcome kya hota hai. Generally, log sochte hain ki human-AI collaboration ka ek average effect hota hai, ya toh achha ya bura. Lekin, yeh research dikhati hai ki baat itni simple nahi hai.

Unhone Polymarket, jo ek real-money prediction market hai, ko use kiya as an objective benchmark. Is pilot study mein pata chala ki human-AI collaboration ki value depend karti hai specific human capital par. Jab individual forecaster ke level par analyze kiya gaya, toh hybrid performance trimodal nikli, matlab teen alag-alag patterns dikhe.

Pehle mode mein, zyada log model ko hi follow karte hain (usko match karte hain). Dusre mode mein, kuch log model ko bas ek rubber-stamp ki tarah use karte hain apne pehle ke guess ko validate karne ke liye, aur ismein unki performance model se bhi kharab ho jaati hai. Lekin, ek chhota group aisa bhi tha jo genuinely complementary reasoning mein engage hua. Yeh log AI ki input ko apne thought process ke saath combine karte hain aur unki accuracy market itself ko match ya exceed kar jaati hai, matlab unka error market se bhi kam hota hai.

Important finding yeh hai ki yeh jo high-performing minority thi, unko raw cognitive ability ya model benchmarks se nahi, balki unke collaborative traits se distinguish kiya gaya. Jaise ki perspective-taking (doosron ka nazariya samajhna), intellectual humility (apni limitations ko accept karna), aur curiosity (seekhne ki ichha). Yeh results abhi preliminary hain, but statistically robust hain, aur aage replication ki taiyari chal rahi hai.

Analyzed at the level of the individual forecaster, hybrid performance is trimodal: most people either deferred to the model (matching it) or used it to rubber-stamp a prior guess (performing worse than the model alone), while a minority engaged in genuine complementary reasoning and reached accuracy matching or even exceeding (i.e., lower error than) the market itself. Collaborative traits (perspective-taking, intellectual humility, and curiosity) rather than raw cognitive ability or model benchmarks, distinguished who reached that mode. The results are preliminary but statistically robust, and motivate a pre-registered replication now in preparation.

Yeh clear nahi hai ki human-AI collaboration kab aur kaise beneficial hoti hai, aur kaun se factors iski success ko drive karte hain.

Method: Researchers ne Polymarket, jo ek real-money prediction market hai, ko ek objective aur externally resolved benchmark ke roop mein use kiya. Unhone individual forecasters ki performance ko analyze kiya jab woh AI ke saath collaborate kar rahe the. Is analysis mein unhone human-AI interaction ke patterns ko identify kiya aur unhe specific human traits ke saath correlate kiya.

Results: Hybrid performance trimodal thi, matlab teen distinct patterns dikhe. Zyada log ya toh model ko follow karte the (matching it) ya phir apne pehle ke guess ko rubber-stamp karte the (performing worse than the model alone). instruction: Explain the following AI research abstract in simple Hinglish.
input:
Title: Learning to Move Before Learning to Do: Task-Agnostic pretraining for VLAs 
Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are fundamentally bottlenecked by the scarcity of expert demonstrations -- triplets of observations, instructions, and actions that are costly to collect at scale. We argue that this bottleneck stems from conflating two distinct learning objectives: acquiring physical competence (how to move) and acquiring semantic alignment (what to do). Crucially, only the latter requires language supervision. Building on this Decomposition Hypothesis, we propose Task-Agnostic Pretraining (TAP), a two-stage framework that first learns transferable motor priors from cheap, unlabeled interaction data -- including discarded off-task trajectories and autonomous robot play -- via a self-supervised Inverse Dynamics objective. A lightweight second stage then grounds these priors in language using minimal expert data. On the SIMPLER benchmark, TAP matches models trained on over 1M expert trajectories while using orders of magnitude less labeled data, yielding a 10% absolute gain over standard behavior cloning. On a real-world WidowX platform, TAP retains 25% success under camera perturbations where internet-scale baselines collapse to 0%, demonstrating that task-agnostic pretraining produces robust, transferable physical representations and offers a scalable path forward for Embodied AI.
output:
VLA models, jo robots ko dekhne, samajhne aur action lene mein help karte hain, unki ek major limitation hai: unhe bahut saari expert demonstrations chahiye hoti hain. Yeh demonstrations – observations, instructions aur actions ke triplets – collect karna bahut costly aur time-consuming hota hai.

Researchers ka kehna hai ki yeh problem isliye aati hai kyunki hum do alag learning objectives ko mix kar dete hain: ek hai physical competence acquire karna (ki robot kaise move kare) aur doosra hai semantic alignment acquire karna (ki robot kya kare). Important baat yeh hai ki sirf 'kya kare' wale part ke liye language supervision ki zaroorat hoti hai.

Is 'Decomposition Hypothesis' par based, unhone Task-Agnostic Pretraining (TAP) naam ka ek two-stage framework propose kiya hai. Pehle stage mein, robot sasta, unlabeled data (jaise ki off-task movements ya khud se play karna) se transferable motor priors seekhta hai. Yeh self-supervised Inverse Dynamics objective use karke hota hai, jisme language ki zaroorat nahi hoti. Dusre stage mein, in seekhe hue motor priors ko minimal expert data aur language supervision ke saath specific tasks ke liye fine-tune kiya jaata hai.

Isse standard Behavior Cloning se 10% ka absolute gain mila. instruction: Explain the following AI research abstract in simple Hinglish.
input:
Title: Will Scaling Improve Social Simulation with LLMs? 
Abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) social simulations are a promising research method, but they are not yet faithful enough to be adopted widely. In this work, we investigate whether the current scaling paradigm in language modeling is likely to close these gaps, or whether simulation fidelity is orthogonal to general capabilities and therefore deserving of more research attention. We use scaling laws to study the relationship between LLMs' compute scale, general capability benchmarks, and the fidelity of social simulation in three representative sub-domains: opinion modeling, behavioral simulation, and longitudinal forecasting. Surprisingly, we discover strong compute scaling in all three settings, using a suite of 85 transformer LLMs with the Qwen3 architecture pre-trained on the DCLM web text corpus under fixed-compute budgets from $10^{18}$ to $10^{20}$ FLOPs. Then we evaluate 35 larger and more capable open-weight models up to 70B parameters, allowing us to predict downstream accuracy from loss. This reveals that the majority of behavioral and opinion simulation tasks will rapidly improve with scale, particularly when they involve populations that are well-represented in English web corpora. Longitudinal forecasting and underrepresented opinions scale more slowly, especially when they are less correlated with general knowledge and reasoning benchmarks like MMLU. In behavior simulation, scaling fails to improve model calibration with human cognitive biases like risk aversion, as well as human heuristics like learning correlated rewards from related tasks. On these tasks, even fine-tuned models fail to noticeably scale up performance from 0.5B to 8B parameters. Taken together, we conclude that scale will improve social simulations in most settings, but outliers exist, and improvements will be less reliable in low-resource domains.
output:
Yeh research paper explore karta hai ki kya Large Language Models (LLMs) ko scale karne se, yaani unhe aur bada aur powerful banane se, social simulations ki accuracy aur reliability improve hogi. Social simulations ka matlab hai LLMs ka use karke human behavior, opinions aur future trends ko simulate karna. Abhi tak, yeh simulations utne accurate nahi hain ki unhe extensively use kiya jaa sake.

Researchers ne yeh investigate kiya ki kya LLMs ki general capabilities ko badhane se (jaise compute power aur model size increase karna) simulation ki fidelity bhi badhegi. Unhone scaling laws ka use kiya aur 85 Qwen3 transformer LLMs ko $10^{18}$ se $10^{20}$ FLOPs ke compute budget par train kiya. Phir 35 bade open-weight models ko bhi evaluate kiya, jo 70 Billion parameters tak the.

Results ne dikhaya ki opinion modeling, behavioral simulation, aur longitudinal forecasting, teeno domains mein strong compute scaling dekhi gayi. Iska matlab hai ki zyada compute aur bade models se performance improve hoti hai. Especially, jo tasks English web corpora mein well-represented populations se related hain, unmein behavioral aur opinion simulation tasks bahut tezi se improve hote hain.

Lekin, kuch exceptions bhi hain. Longitudinal forecasting aur underrepresented opinions wale tasks dheere scale karte hain, khaaskar jab woh MMLU jaise general knowledge benchmarks se kam correlated hon. Aur behavioral simulation mein, human cognitive biases jaise risk aversion ya human heuristics ko simulate karne mein scaling se koi khaas improvement nahi mili, even fine-tuned models mein bhi. Toh conclusion yeh hai ki scale karne se social simulations generally improve honge, but kuch specific cases mein, khaaskar low-resource domains mein, improvements utne reliable nahi honge.

instruction: Break down the following AI research abstract into Problem, Method and Results in simple Hinglish.
input:
Title: Will Scaling Improve Social Simulation with LLMs? 
Abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) social simulations are a promising research method, but they are not yet faithful enough to be adopted widely. In this work, we investigate whether the current scaling paradigm in language modeling is likely to close these gaps, or whether simulation fidelity is orthogonal to general capabilities and therefore deserving of more research attention. We use scaling laws to study the relationship between LLMs' compute scale, general capability benchmarks, and the fidelity of social simulation in three representative sub-domains: opinion modeling, behavioral simulation, and longitudinal forecasting. Surprisingly, we discover strong compute scaling in all three settings, using a suite of 85 transformer LLMs with the Qwen3 architecture pre-trained on the DCLM web text corpus under fixed-compute budgets from $10^{18}$ to $10^{20}$ FLOPs. Then we evaluate 35 larger and more capable open-weight models up to 70B parameters, allowing us to predict downstream accuracy from loss. This reveals that the majority of behavioral and opinion simulation tasks will rapidly improve with scale, particularly when they involve populations that are well-represented in English web corpora. Longitudinal forecasting and underrepresented opinions scale more slowly, especially when they are less correlated with general knowledge and reasoning benchmarks like MMLU. In behavior simulation, scaling fails to improve model calibration with human cognitive biases like risk aversion, as well as human heuristics like learning correlated rewards from related tasks. On these tasks, even fine-tuned models fail to noticeably scale up performance from 0.5B to 8B parameters. Taken together, we conclude that scale will improve social simulations in most settings, but outliers exist, and improvements will be less reliable in low-resource domains.
output:
Problem: LLM social simulations ek promising method hai, but unki fidelity (accuracy) abhi itni nahi hai ki unhe widely adopt kiya jaa sake. Core challenge yeh hai ki kya LLMs ko scale karne se (unhe aur bada aur powerful banane se) yeh fidelity gap close hoga, ya phir simulation fidelity ek alag research area hai jo general capabilities se independent hai.

Method: Researchers ne scaling laws ka use kiya to study the relationship between LLMs' compute scale, general capability benchmarks, aur social simulation fidelity. Unhone do primary setups use kiye:
1. 85 transformer LLMs (Qwen3 architecture, DCLM web text corpus) ko $10^{18}$ se $10^{20}$ FLOPs ke fixed-compute budgets par train kiya.
2. Phir 35 larger aur more capable open-weight models (up to 70B parameters) ko evaluate kiya, to predict downstream accuracy from loss. Yeh study teen sub-domains mein ki gayi: opinion modeling, behavioral simulation, aur longitudinal forecasting.

Results: Surprisingly, teeno settings mein strong compute scaling dekhi gayi. Majority of behavioral aur opinion simulation tasks scale ke saath rapidly improve hote hain, khaaskar jab woh English web corpora mein well-represented populations se related hon. Longitudinal forecasting aur underrepresented opinions dheere scale karte hain, especially jab woh MMLU jaise general knowledge benchmarks se kam correlated hon. Behavioral simulation mein, scaling human cognitive biases (jaise risk aversion) aur heuristics ko improve karne mein fail ho gaya; fine-tuned models (0.5B se 8B parameters) mein bhi koi noticeable scale-up nahi mila. Conclusion yeh hai ki scale generally social simulations ko improve karega, but outliers exist karte hain, aur low-resource domains mein improvements kam reliable honge. The abstract does not explicitly mention specific quantitative accuracy numbers or benchmark scores.

instruction: Explain the following AI research abstract in simple Hinglish.
input:
Title: OrbitQuant: Data-Agnostic Quantization for Image and Video Diffusion Transformers 
Abstract: Diffusion transformers (DiTs) achieve state-of-the-art image and video generation, but their multi-step sampling and growing parameter count make inference expensive. Post-training quantization (PTQ) is the natural remedy, yet DiT activations shift across timesteps, prompts, and guidance branches, forcing prior methods to re-fit calibration data for every new checkpoint or modality. We present OrbitQuant, a data-agnostic weight-activation quantizer that bypasses range estimation by quantizing in a normalized, rotated basis. In this basis, a randomized permuted block-Hadamard (RPBH) rotation concentrates each coordinate around one fixed, known marginal regardless of the input, so a single Lloyd-Max codebook serves all timesteps, prompts, and layers of a given input dimension. We extend the same quantizer to weight rows offline, absorbing the rotation into the weights so that it cancels inside each linear layer and only a forward rotation on the activations remains at runtime. The same recipe transfers from image to video with no per-modality tuning. Across FLUX.1, Z-Image-Turbo, Wan 2.1, and CogVideoX, it sets the state of the art for PTQ at several low-bit settings. It also pushes PTQ of image diffusion transformers to W2A4 with usable generation quality.
output:
Students, aaj hum OrbitQuant paper discuss karenge. DiTs, yaani Diffusion Transformers, aajkal image aur video generation mein sabse best hain. Lekin, inka inference, matlab jab hum in models ko use karte hain kuch generate karne ke liye, bahut expensive ho jaata hai. Kyunki inmein multi-step sampling hoti hai aur parameter count bhi bahut zyada hota hai.

Is problem ko solve karne ke liye Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) ek common approach hai. Ismein model ke bade numbers ko chhote numbers mein convert karte hain, jisse model lightweight aur fast ho jaata hai. Lekin DiTs ke saath ek issue hai: unke activations, jo internal data representations hote hain, alag-alag timesteps, prompts aur guidance branches par change hote rehte hain. Is wajah se purane PTQ methods ko har naye checkpoint ya modality ke liye calibration data ko baar-baar re-fit karna padta tha, jo ki practical nahi tha.

OrbitQuant is problem ka solution hai. Yeh ek data-agnostic weight-activation quantizer hai. Iska matlab hai ki isko quantization ke liye calibration data ki zaroorat nahi padti. Yeh ek naye tareeke se quantize karta hai: ek 'normalized, rotated basis' mein. Is basis mein, ek special rotation technique, jise Randomized Permuted Block-Hadamard (RPBH) rotation kehte hain, har coordinate ko ek 'fixed, known marginal' ke around concentrate kar deti hai, chahe input kuch bhi ho. Isse ek single Lloyd-Max codebook saare timesteps, prompts aur layers ke liye use ho sakta hai.

Weights ke liye bhi yehi quantizer use hota hai, but offline. Rotation ko weights mein absorb kar liya jaata hai, taki linear layer ke andar woh cancel ho jaaye aur runtime par sirf activations par forward rotation apply ho. Is method ki khaas baat yeh hai ki yeh image se video generation tak bina kisi extra tuning ke kaam karta hai. Isne kai models jaise FLUX.1 aur CogVideoX par low-bit settings mein state-of-the-art results achieve kiye hain, aur W2A4 (2-bit weights, 4-bit activations) par bhi usable quality provide ki hai.

instruction: Explain the following AI research abstract in simple Hinglish.
input:
Title: Neuron-Aware Data Selection for Annotation-Free LLM Self-Distillation 
Abstract: Post-training large language models (LLMs) without real-world interaction feedback or human-labeled supervision remains challenging, particularly in specialized domains where expert annotations are costly to obtain. Recent annotation-free self-evolution methods address this by using the model's own outputs as supervision signals, constructing a teacher via additional context and aggregating predictions across multiple rollouts through majority voting to produce pseudo-labels. However, these approaches are not without drawbacks: SFT- and GRPO-based variants suffer out-of-domain performance degradation, while reward-based on-policy RL inflates calibration error. In this paper, we propose Neuron On-Policy Self-Distillation (Neuron-OPSD), a data-centric framework for annotation-free self-distillation that leverages internal neuron activations to guide both training-data selection and teacher context construction. The model is then trained via on-policy distillation from the teacher distribution, requiring no ground-truth labels at any stage. Across specialized-domain benchmarks, Neuron-OPSD improves in-domain task performance while preserving cross-domain generalization and mitigating calibration collapse over prior annotation-free baselines. This framework is particularly relevant to settings where online interaction or external supervision is costly or infeasible, and is conceptually distinct from offline RL approaches that rely on logged, reward-labeled trajectories.
output:
Large Language Models (LLMs) ko train karna without real-world interaction feedback ya human-labeled supervision bahut challenging hota hai, especially jab baat specialized domains ki ho. Aise domains mein expert annotations collect karna bahut costly hota hai.

Recent annotation-free self-evolution methods is problem ko address karte hain by using the model ke apne outputs ko hi supervision signals ke roop mein. Ismein ek 'teacher' model banaya jaata hai additional context dekar, aur multiple rollouts se predictions ko aggregate karke pseudo-labels generate kiye jaate hain.

Lekin, in approaches mein kuch drawbacks hain. Jaise, SFT- aur GRPO-based variants out-of-domain performance mein degrade karte hain, aur reward-based on-policy Reinforcement Learning (RL) calibration error ko badha deta hai.

Is paper mein, hum Neuron On-Policy Self-Distillation (Neuron-OPSD) propose karte hain. Yeh ek data-centric framework hai annotation-free self-distillation ke liye. Iska main idea hai ki yeh model ke internal neuron activations ko use karta hai. In activations ki help se, yeh framework training-data selection aur teacher context construction dono ko guide karta hai.

Model ko phir is teacher distribution se on-policy distillation ke through train kiya jaata hai, aur is poore process mein koi ground-truth labels ki zaroorat nahi padti. Specialized-domain benchmarks par, Neuron-OPSD in-domain task performance improve karta hai, cross-domain generalization maintain karta hai, aur pehle ke annotation-free baselines ke comparison mein calibration collapse ko bhi kam karta hai. Yeh framework un settings ke liye bahut relevant hai jahan online interaction ya external supervision costly ya infeasible hai.

instruction: What are the main engineering or algorithmic key takeaways from this paper?
input:
Title: Neuron-Aware Data Selection for Annotation-Free LLM Self-Distillation 
Abstract: Post-training large language models (LLMs) without real-world interaction feedback or human-labeled supervision remains challenging, particularly in specialized domains where expert annotations are costly to obtain. Recent annotation-free self-evolution methods address this by using the model's own outputs as supervision signals, constructing a teacher via additional context and aggregating predictions across multiple rollouts through majority voting to produce pseudo-labels. However, these approaches are not without drawbacks: SFT- and GRPO-based variants suffer out-of-domain performance degradation, while reward-based on-policy RL inflates calibration error. In this paper, we propose Neuron On-Policy Self-Distillation (Neuron-OPSD), a data-centric framework for annotation-free self-distillation that leverages internal neuron activations to guide both training-data selection and teacher context construction. The model is then trained via on-policy distillation from the teacher distribution, requiring no ground-truth labels at any stage. Across specialized-domain benchmarks, Neuron-OPSD improves in-domain task performance while preserving cross-domain generalization and mitigating calibration collapse over prior annotation-free baselines. This framework is particularly relevant to settings where online interaction or external supervision is costly or infeasible, and is conceptually distinct from offline RL approaches that rely on logged, reward-labeled trajectories.
output:
Is paper se kuch primary engineering aur algorithmic takeaways hain:

1.  **Leveraging Internal Neuron Activations for Data-Centricity:** The core innovation is using internal neuron activations. Yeh ek novel approach hai data selection aur teacher context construction ko guide karne ke liye. Previously, annotation-free methods primarily focused on aggregating model outputs. Neuron-OPSD shows that internal model states can provide richer signals for self-improvement, moving beyond just output-level supervision.

2.  **Annotation-Free Self-Distillation:** The framework enables effective self-distillation without any ground-truth labels. This is crucial for specialized domains where expert annotations are scarce or expensive. It signifies a step towards more autonomous LLM training paradigms, reducing reliance on costly human effort.

3.  **Mitigating Prior Method Drawbacks:** Neuron-OPSD specifically addresses the limitations of previous annotation-free baselines. It improves in-domain performance, jo specialized tasks ke liye vital hai, while also preserving cross-domain generalization. Importantly, it mitigates calibration collapse, making the model's confidence scores more reliable, which is a significant engineering concern for real-world deployments.

4.  **On-Policy Distillation Strategy:** The method employs on-policy distillation from a teacher distribution. This implies that the model learns from a teacher jo continuously updated ya adapted hota hai based on the current policy, rather than a static teacher. This dynamic learning approach often leads to more robust and effective training.

5.  **Distinction from Offline RL:** The paper explicitly highlights its conceptual distinction from offline Reinforcement Learning. While both deal with limited external interaction, Neuron-OPSD focuses on generating supervision *internally* without relying on pre-logged, reward-labeled trajectories, which is a different problem setting and solution space.

instruction: Explain the following AI research abstract in simple Hinglish.
input:
Title: Language Models as Measurement Apparatus for Culture 
Abstract: Language models are increasingly used to quantify cultural phenomena, but what makes such measurement distinctively cultural? This paper argues that NLP work on culture is a material-discursive practice: the apparatus -- model, data, annotation, evaluation -- participates in constituting the cultural reality it measures, rather than passively recording it. Drawing on Karen Barad's concept of the agential cut -- the contingent boundary between phenomenon and instrument -- I show that the apparatus's substantive design choices draw such boundaries, and that the boundary is entangled from the start because language models have already internalized much of the cultural material they measure. I illustrate this through three case studies on television and film dialogue (measuring structure, interaction, and deviation) and three examinations of the apparatus itself (erasure of cultural markers, attunement to historical material, and agency in an agentic workflow). This big picture analysis proposes a research program that is theory-driven, empirically rigorous, and culturally contingent, treating each agential cut as a conscious commitment, at once methodological and ethical.
output:
Language Models (LMs) aajkal cultural phenomena ko quantify karne ke liye kaafi use ho rahe hain. Lekin, yeh paper question karta hai ki is measurement ko 'distinctively cultural' kya banata hai. Paper argue karta hai ki NLP work on culture ek 'material-discursive practice' hai. Iska matlab hai ki jo apparatus hum use karte hain – jaise model, data, annotation, aur evaluation – woh khud us cultural reality ko banata hai jise woh measure kar raha hai, na ki sirf use passively record karta hai. 

Karen Barad ke 'agential cut' concept ko use karte hue, paper dikhata hai ki phenomenon aur instrument ke beech ki boundary contingent hoti hai. Apparatus ke design choices hi yeh boundaries banate hain. Yeh boundary shuru se hi entangled hoti hai, kyunki LMs ne already bahut saara cultural material internalize kar liya hota hai jise woh measure kar rahe hain. 

Is point ko illustrate karne ke liye, paper ne teen case studies kiye hain television aur film dialogue par, jahan structure, interaction, aur deviation ko measure kiya gaya. Saath hi, apparatus ke teen examinations bhi kiye gaye hain: cultural markers ka erasure, historical material se attunement, aur agentic workflow mein agency. Overall, yeh analysis ek research program propose karta hai jo theory-driven, empirically rigorous, aur culturally contingent hai, jahan har 'agential cut' ko ek conscious commitment mana jaata hai, jo methodological aur ethical dono hai.

instruction: Explain the following AI research abstract in simple Hinglish.
input:
Title: Understanding the Robustness of Distributed Self-Supervised Learning Frameworks Against Non-IID Data 
Abstract: Recent research has introduced distributed self-supervised learning (D-SSL) approaches to leverage vast amounts of unlabeled decentralized data. However, D-SSL faces the critical challenge of data heterogeneity, and there is limited theoretical understanding of how different D-SSL frameworks respond to this challenge. To fill this gap, we present a rigorous theoretical analysis of the robustness of D-SSL frameworks under non-IID (non-independent and identically distributed) settings. Our results show that pre-training with Masked Image Modeling (MIM) is inherently more robust to heterogeneous data than Contrastive Learning (CL), and that the robustness of decentralized SSL increases with average network connectivity, implying that federated learning (FL) is no less robust than decentralized learning (DecL). These findings provide a solid theoretical foundation for guiding the design of future D-SSL algorithms. To further illustrate the practical implications of our theory, we introduce MAR loss, a refinement of the MIM objective with local-to-global alignment regularization. Extensive experiments across model architectures and distributed settings validate our theoretical insights, and additionally confirm the effectiveness of MAR loss as an application of our analysis.
output:
Toh students, yeh paper Distributed Self-Supervised Learning (D-SSL) ke ek bahut important aspect par focus karta hai. D-SSL mein hum scattered, unlabeled data ko use karke models train karte hain, jo ki ek bahut powerful approach hai. Lekin ismein ek major challenge aata hai data heterogeneity ka, jise hum non-IID data bhi kehte hain. Iska matlab hai ki jo data different locations par hai, woh ek jaisa distributed nahi hota, usmein kaafi variations hote hain.

Paper ka main goal hai is heterogeneity ke against D-SSL frameworks ki robustness ko theoretically analyze karna. Matlab, yeh dekhna ki non-IID data hone par bhi model kitna stable aur effective rehta hai. Researchers ne yahan ek rigorous theoretical analysis perform kiya hai.

Unhone do popular self-supervised learning methods ko compare kiya: Masked Image Modeling (MIM) aur Contrastive Learning (CL). Unki findings se pata chala ki MIM, heterogeneous data ke liye CL se inherently zyada robust hai. Yeh ek significant insight hai. Dusra important result yeh hai ki decentralized SSL ki robustness network connectivity ke average level ke saath badhti hai. Iska matlab hai ki agar nodes ke beech connectivity achhi hai, toh model zyada robust hoga. Isse yeh bhi pata chalta hai ki Federated Learning (FL), jo high connectivity par based hai, Decentralized Learning (DecL) se kam robust nahi hai.

Yeh theoretical insights future D-SSL algorithms design karne ke liye ek strong foundation provide karte hain. Apni theory ko practical level par demonstrate karne ke liye, paper ne MAR loss introduce kiya hai, jo MIM objective ka ek refinement hai. Is loss function mein local-to-global alignment regularization add kiya gaya hai. Experiments ne inki theoretical findings ko validate kiya hai aur MAR loss ki effectiveness ko bhi confirm kiya hai.

To further illustrate the practical implications of our theory, we introduce MAR loss, a refinement of the MIM objective with local-to-global alignment regularization. Extensive experiments across model architectures and distributed settings validate our theoretical insights, and additionally confirm the effectiveness of MAR loss as an application of our analysis.

instruction: Explain the following AI research abstract in simple Hinglish.
input:
Title: Optimal Stabilizer Testing and Learning with Limited Quantum Memory 
Abstract: We study stabilizer state testing and learning with limited coherent quantum memory. Here an algorithm sequentially receives copies of an unknown $n$-qubit state, but may keep only $k$ qubits of coherent quantum memory between measurements. With unrestricted memory, seminal work of Gross, Nezami and Walter showed how to test $n$-qubit stabilizer states using $6$ copies, which is dimension independent, unlike the learning complexity of $Θ(n)$. We show that this testing-vs-learning separation is lost under memory constraints. More concretely we show that   (1) The sample complexity of testing stabilizer states in the $k$-qubit memory framework is $Θ(n-k)$. Our upper bound goes via a novel connection to the hidden shift problem and the lower bound is proven using a novel approach to average case bounds on likelihood ratios via combinatorics of the stochastic orthogonal group.   (2) The sample complexity of learning stabilizer states with $k$ qubits of memory, in the non-adaptive framework, is $Θ(n^2/k)$.   As a further application of our techniques, we prove an exponential lower bound for purity testing even when the memory may be left coherent throughout the protocol. Our main results identify coherent quantum memory as the resource enabling the usual separation between stabilizer testing and learning. In particular, even with $k=0.99n$ qubits of memory, there is no constant-copy stabilizer tester; furthermore for $k=cn$ qubits of memory (for $0< c < 1$), stabilizer testing is as hard as learning, with both requiring $Θ(n)$ copies.
output:
Students, yeh paper quantum computing ke ek fundamental aspect par focus karta hai: Stabilizer states ko test karna aur learn karna, especially jab hamare paas limited coherent quantum memory ho. Stabilizer states quantum information theory mein bahut important hote hain, jaise quantum error correction mein. Normally, agar unlimited memory ho, toh ek stabilizer state ko test karne ke liye sirf 6 copies ki zaroorat hoti hai, irrespective of the number of qubits ($n$). Lekin usko learn karne mein $Θ(n)$ copies lagte hain. Yeh ek significant 'testing-vs-learning separation' hai.

Lekin, yeh research dikhata hai ki jab memory limited ho (yani aap sirf $k$ qubits ki coherent memory store kar sakte ho measurements ke beech), toh yeh separation khatam ho jaati hai. Specifically, agar aapko stabilizer states test karne hain $k$-qubit memory ke saath, toh sample complexity $Θ(n-k)$ ho jaati hai. Aur agar learn karna hai, non-adaptive framework mein, toh sample complexity $Θ(n^2/k)$ ho jaati hai. Iska matlab hai ki memory constraints ke chalte, testing bhi utna hi difficult ho jaata hai jitna learning, especially jab $k$ bahut chhota ho ya $k$ ek fraction ho $n$ ka. Paper yeh bhi prove karta hai ki coherent quantum memory hi woh resource hai jo is separation ko enable karta hai. Even agar aapke paas almost $n$ qubits ki memory ho (jaise $k=0.99n$), tab bhi constant-copy tester possible nahi hai. Yeh findings quantum algorithms design karne mein bahut crucial hain.

instruction: Explain the following AI research abstract in simple Hinglish.
input:
Title: EvoPolicyGym: Evaluating Autonomous Policy Evolution in Interactive Environments 
Abstract: Autonomous agents are increasingly expected to improve executable policies through feedback, yet existing evaluations often collapse this process into a final score or confound it with open-ended software-engineering progress. We introduce Autonomous Policy Evolution, a controlled evaluation setting in which a harness-model agent repeatedly edits an executable policy system under a fixed interaction budget. We instantiate this setting in EvoPolicyGym, a benchmark built from compact interactive RL environments that evaluates how agents iteratively improve explored policies. On the EvoPolicyGym suite, GPT-5.5 achieves the strongest aggregate rank score and top-two performance on all 16 environments. Beyond leaderboard results, EvoPolicyGym also provides trajectory-level diagnostics that distinguish how agents allocate budget, convert feedback into parametric tuning. These analyses show that strong autonomous policy evolution depends not only on isolated task wins, but on discovering task-appropriate mechanisms and refining policies under bounded feedback.

Yeh approach utni effective nahi hai.

Is paper mein, researchers ne 'Autonomous Policy Evolution' (APE) naam ka ek controlled evaluation setting introduce kiya hai. Ismein ek 'harness-model agent' hota hai, jo ek executable policy system ko baar-baar edit karta hai. Yeh sab ek fixed interaction budget ke andar hota hai. Matlab, agent ko ek limited number of tries ya interactions milte hain policies ko improve karne ke liye.

Is setting ko implement karne ke liye, unhone 'EvoPolicyGym' banaya hai. Yeh ek benchmark hai jismein compact interactive Reinforcement Learning (RL) environments hain. Iska main maqsad yeh dekhna hai ki agents kaise iteratively apni policies ko improve karte hain, feedback ka use karke. Sirf final score nahi, balki poora evolution process important hai.

instruction: Break down the following AI research abstract into Problem, Method and Results in simple Hinglish.
input:
Title: EvoPolicyGym: Evaluating Autonomous Policy Evolution in Interactive Environments 
Abstract: Autonomous agents are increasingly expected to improve executable policies through feedback, yet existing evaluations often collapse this process into a final score or confound it with open-ended software-engineering progress. We introduce Autonomous Policy Evolution, a controlled evaluation setting in which a harness-model agent repeatedly edits an executable policy system under a fixed interaction budget. We instantiate this setting in EvoPolicyGym, a benchmark built from compact interactive RL environments that evaluates how agents iteratively improve explored policies. On the EvoPolicyGym suite, GPT-5.5 achieves the strongest aggregate rank score and top-two performance on all 16 environments. Beyond leaderboard results, EvoPolicyGym also provides trajectory-level diagnostics that distinguish how agents allocate budget, convert feedback into parametric tuning. These analyses show that strong autonomous policy evolution depends not only on isolated task wins, but on discovering task-appropriate mechanisms and refining policies under bounded feedback.

instruction: Explain the following AI research abstract in simple Hinglish.
input:
Title: Extreme Adaptive Transformer for Time Series Forecasting 
Abstract: Time series forecasting remains challenging when the underlying data contain rare but critical extreme events. This issue is particularly important in hydrologic forecasting, where streamflow distributions are often highly skewed and extreme peaks can have substantial impacts on flood monitoring, water resource management, and early warning systems. Although Transformer-based forecasting models have achieved strong performance by modeling long-range temporal dependencies, they typically treat all time points uniformly and may therefore underrepresent rare extreme patterns. In this paper, we propose the Extreme-Adaptive Transformer (Exformer), a forecasting framework designed to explicitly model temporal dependencies involving both normal and extreme events. Exformer introduces an extreme-adaptive attention mechanism composed of three sparse components: Local, Stride, and Extreme. The Local and Stride components capture short-term and periodic temporal dependencies, respectively, while the Extreme component selectively models event-aware dependencies between normal and extreme streamflow patterns. Experiments on four real-world hydrologic streamflow datasets show that Exformer achieves superior 3-day forecasting performance compared with state-of-the-art baselines. Our findings demonstrate that explicitly incorporating extreme-aware attention improves the forecasting capacity of Transformer models on imbalanced time series with rare but consequential events.
output:
Students, yeh paper time series forecasting ke ek important challenge ko address karta hai. Jab data mein rare, yaani kabhi-kabhi hone wale, but critical extreme events hote hain, toh unhe forecast karna mushkil ho jaata hai. Jaise, hydrologic forecasting mein, jahan streamflow (nadi ka paani ka flow) kaafi skewed hota hai aur extreme peaks (bahut zyaada paani) floods laa sakte hain ya water resource management ko affect kar sakte hain. Existing Transformer models long-range dependencies ko achhe se handle karte hain, but woh sabhi time points ko equally treat karte hain. Isse woh rare extreme patterns ko theek se represent nahi kar paate.

Is problem ko solve karne ke liye, yeh paper 'Extreme-Adaptive Transformer' yaani Exformer propose karta hai. Exformer ka main aim hai normal aur extreme events dono ke temporal dependencies ko explicitly model karna. Iske liye, Exformer ek special 'extreme-adaptive attention mechanism' use karta hai, jiske teen sparse components hain: Local, Stride, aur Extreme. Local component short-term dependencies ko dekhta hai, Stride component periodic dependencies ko capture karta hai, aur sabse important, Extreme component selectively normal aur extreme streamflow patterns ke beech event-aware dependencies ko model karta hai.

Experiments mein, Exformer ne four real-world hydrologic streamflow datasets par superior 3-day forecasting performance dikhayi hai, jo state-of-the-art baselines se better hai. Isse yeh prove hota hai ki extreme-aware attention ko explicitly incorporate karne se Transformer models ki forecasting capacity significantly improve hoti hai, especially for imbalanced time series jahan rare events kaafi consequential hote hain.

instruction: Explain the following AI research abstract in simple Hinglish.
input:
Title: Reasoning effort, not tool access, buys first-try reliability in agentic code generation: an observational study 
Abstract: Agentic coding assistants are increasingly given extra capabilities, such as browser based testing tools and design oriented system prompts, on the assumption that more capability yields better software. This study tested that assumption directly. Ninety independent agent runs built the same application, a real time retrospective board, from one detailed specification, each scored on a fixed 14 criterion functional rubric (42 point maximum) and a visual quality review. The runs spanned several model generations, two agent harnesses, two reasoning effort levels, a testing tool, and two design oriented prompts. Capability tier dominated: frontier models clustered near the ceiling while a low cost local model fell to 24 to 37 points. A criterion level analysis revealed what run totals conceal. Container deployment was the dominant defect, failing first try in 44 percent of runs, with its failure rate shifting sharply across model generations while mean totals moved less than a point. The testing tool raised cost by 42 to 68 percent without improving functional score or reliability, even on interface visible criteria. Raising reasoning effort from High to xHigh lifted first try perfect runs from 28 percent to 89 percent and cut corrective prompts about five fold, for 9 to 29 percent more cost. A design oriented prompt raised visual quality, 4.5 versus 3.0 on a 5 point scale, without lifting function, and a one paragraph paraphrase of its directive reproduced the entire lift. The practical lesson is to match the fix to the failure: most first run failures came from weak reasoning, which a stronger model or more effort prevents, not from visible flaws a checking tool would catch.
output:
Yeh research paper agentic coding assistants ke capabilities par focus karta hai. Generally, hum sochte hain ki agar AI agents ko zyada tools, jaise browser based testing tools ya design prompts, diye jaayen toh woh better software banayenge. Is study ne isi assumption ko directly test kiya.

Unhone ek hi application, ek real-time retrospective board, banwane ke liye 90 independent agent runs kiye. Har run ko 14 functional criteria (total 42 points) aur visual quality par score kiya gaya. Experiment mein kai factors vary kiye gaye, jaise alag-alag model generations, agent harnesses, do reasoning effort levels (High se xHigh), testing tool ka use, aur design oriented prompts.

Results kaafi interesting the. Capability tier bahut important nikla: jo frontier models the, unhone highest scores achieve kiye, jabki ek low-cost local model ka score 24 se 37 points ke beech raha. Ek major finding yeh tha ki container deployment sabse bada defect tha, jo 44% runs mein first try mein fail ho gaya.

Sabse critical baat yeh hai ki testing tool ne cost ko 42% se 68% tak badha diya, lekin functional score ya reliability mein koi improvement nahi laaya, even interface visible criteria par bhi nahi. Iske opposite, reasoning effort ko High se xHigh karne se first-try perfect runs 28% se badhkar 89% ho gaye aur corrective prompts paanch guna kam ho gaye, although ismein 9% se 29% extra cost laga.

Design oriented prompts ne visual quality ko improve kiya (5 mein se 4.5 vs 3.0), lekin functional aspects par koi asar nahi pada. Iska main lesson yeh hai ki failures ko fix karne ke liye sahi approach choose karna chahiye: zyadaतर first-run failures weak reasoning ki wajah se hote hain, jise ek stronger model ya zyada reasoning effort se theek kiya ja sakta hai, na ki sirf external checking tools se.

instruction: Break down the following AI research abstract into Problem, Method and Results in simple Hinglish.
input:
Title: Reasoning effort, not tool access, buys first-try reliability in agentic code generation: an observational study 
Abstract: Agentic coding assistants are increasingly given extra capabilities, such as browser based testing tools and design oriented system prompts, on the assumption that more capability yields better software. This study tested that assumption directly. Ninety independent agent runs built the same application, a real time retrospective board, from one detailed specification, each scored on a fixed 14 criterion functional rubric (42 point maximum) and a visual quality review. The runs spanned several model generations, two agent harnesses, two reasoning effort levels, a testing tool, and two design oriented prompts. Capability tier dominated: frontier models clustered near the ceiling while a low cost local model fell to 24 to 37 points. A criterion level analysis revealed what run totals conceal. Container deployment was the dominant defect, failing first try in 44 percent of runs, with its failure rate shifting sharply across model generations while mean totals moved less than a point. The testing tool raised cost by 42 to 68 percent without improving functional score or reliability, even on interface visible criteria. Raising reasoning effort from High to xHigh lifted first try perfect runs from 28 percent to 89 percent and cut corrective prompts about five fold, for 9 to 29 percent more cost. A design oriented prompt raised visual quality, 4.5 versus 3.0 on a 5 point scale, without lifting function, and a one paragraph paraphrase of its directive reproduced the entire lift. The practical lesson is to match the fix to the failure: most first run failures came from weak reasoning, which a stronger model or more effort prevents, not from visible flaws a checking tool would catch.

Problem: Industry mein yeh assumption hai ki agentic coding assistants ko zyada capabilities (jaise testing tools aur design prompts) dene se automatically better software banta hai. Is study ka core problem isi assumption ko directly test karna tha, aur yeh pata karna tha ki kya yeh assumption sahi hai.

Method: Researchers ne ek observational study conduct ki. Ismein, 90 independent agent runs ne ek hi application, ek real-time retrospective board, banaya, jo ek detailed specification par based tha. Har run ko 14-criterion functional rubric (42 points max) aur visual quality review par score kiya gaya. Experiment mein kai variables ko vary kiya gaya: alag-alag model generations, do agent harnesses, do reasoning effort levels (High aur xHigh), ek testing tool ka use, aur do design oriented prompts.

Results:
*   Model capability tier bahut important nikla: Frontier models ne high scores achieve kiye, jabki low-cost local models ne 24 se 37 points score kiye.
*   Container deployment sabse dominant defect tha, jo 44% runs mein first try mein fail ho gaya.
*   Testing tool ne cost ko 42% se 68% tak badha diya, lekin functional score ya reliability mein koi improvement nahi laaya.
*   Reasoning effort ko High se xHigh karne se first-try perfect runs 28% se badhkar 89% ho gaye aur corrective prompts paanch guna kam ho gaye, ismein 9% se 29% extra cost laga.

instruction: Explain the following AI research abstract in simple Hinglish.
input:
Title: MARVEL: Margin-Aware Robust von Mises-Fischer Expert Learning for Long-Tailed Out-of-Distribution Detection 
Abstract: For clinical deployment, it is essential that automated diagnostic systems remain reliable when confronted with previously unseen cases, yet deep models routinely misclassify out-of-distribution (OOD) inputs with high confidence, underscoring the need for more robust OOD detection methods. Although substantial effort has been devoted to improving model robustness, most of the existing literature assumes balanced datasets, evaluates OOD detection on coarse or non-clinical OOD sources, or lacks comprehensive assessment across diverse OOD scenarios. To address the gaps, we propose a novel methodology trained on diverse and imbalanced medical datasets and evaluated across a clinically reflective OOD spectrum. Our framework comprises three key components: (1) a Nonlinear von Mises-Fisher (NvMF) classifier capable of learning non-linear decision boundaries, with theoretical proof of its asymptotic connection to cosine classifiers; (2) a multi-expert framework in which margin-aware NvMF classifiers specialise in different regions of label distribution to better handle imbalance; and (3) an outlier expert trained explicitly to distinguish inlier from outlier data, thereby strengthening OOD detection. Evaluation on RFMiD, ISIC2019, and NCTCRC datasets demonstrates consistent improvements over state-of-the-art methods, achieving mean FPR95 reductions of 8.45%, 13.02%, and 36.90% respectively. These gains are further supported by comprehensive ablations that validated the contributions of each component. This enables reliable identification of unfamiliar cases for deferral to clinicians, supporting safer AI-assisted diagnosis in real-world workflows. Our code is available at https://github.com/redboxup/MARVEL.
output:
Students, yeh paper MARVEL, medical diagnosis mein AI ki reliability improve karne ke liye hai. Generally, deep learning models ko jab koi 'Out-of-Distribution' (OOD) data milta hai, matlab jo unhone pehle dekha nahi hai, toh woh use galat classify kar dete hain, aur woh bhi high confidence ke saath. Clinical settings mein yeh bahut risky hai, kyunki ek unseen disease ko normal diagnose karna patient ke liye dangerous ho sakta hai.

Existing methods mein problem yeh hai ki woh mostly balanced datasets par kaam karte hain, ya unka OOD detection real-world clinical scenarios ke liye robust nahi hota. Is gap ko fill karne ke liye, MARVEL ek naya framework propose karta hai jo diverse aur imbalanced medical datasets par train hota hai.

Iske teen main components hain: Pehla, ek 'Nonlinear von Mises-Fisher (NvMF) classifier' jo complex, non-linear decision boundaries learn kar sakta hai. Iska theoretical connection cosine classifiers se bhi hai. Dusra, ek 'multi-expert framework' jismein alag-alag NvMF classifiers, label distribution ke different regions mein specialize karte hain, especially long-tailed ya imbalanced data ko better handle karne ke liye. Aur teesra, ek dedicated 'outlier expert' jo explicitly inlier aur outlier data ko distinguish karta hai, jisse OOD detection bahut strong ho jaata hai.

Is approach se, system unfamiliar cases ko reliably identify kar pata hai aur unhe clinicians ko refer kar sakta hai, making AI-assisted diagnosis much safer.

instruction: Explain the following AI research abstract in simple Hinglish.
input:
Title: Automated grading of Linux/bash examinations using large language models: a four-level cognitive taxonomy approach 
Abstract: Scalable and reliable grading of command-line examinations remains a challenge in computing education, where rising enrolments make manual marking difficult and rule-based autograders cannot handle partial credit, equivalent solutions, or syntactic variation. This paper evaluates whether four frontier Large Language Models (GPT, Claude Opus, Gemini, and GLM) can approximate expert judgment when grading short Linux/bash command responses. The study adopts a four-level cognitive taxonomy that combines cognitive complexity and operational impact, ranging from information retrieval (L1) and basic file manipulation (L2) to structural operations (L3) and advanced system management (L4). The models were tested with two prompt variants, a minimal baseline and a rubric-enhanced version, on 1200 real responses from second-year Computer Engineering students independently graded by three expert instructors. Gemini~3.0 Pro with rubric-guided prompting achieved the highest human-AI agreement (ICC(3,1) = 0.888, MAE = 0.10, Bland-Altman bias = -0.014). Agreement declined consistently as taxonomy level increased, with the largest discrepancies at higher levels. Across all models, rubric quality had a larger effect than provider choice, with structured prompts consistently improving agreement. These results show that question complexity is a reliable predictor of the difficulty LLMs face in grading accurately, and they establish a principled, taxonomy-based framework for determining which questions are suitable for AI-assisted grading and which require human review, while also providing a transferable evaluation protocol and prompt templates.
output:
Students ke Linux/bash exams ko grade karna, especially jab enrollments badh rahe hain, ek challenging task hai. Manual grading time-consuming hai aur existing rule-based autograders partial credit, equivalent solutions, ya syntactic variations ko properly handle nahi kar paate. Is research paper mein, researchers ne explore kiya ki kya Large Language Models (LLMs) jaise GPT, Claude Opus, Gemini, aur GLM, expert instructors ki tarah grading kar sakte hain.

Unhone ek four-level cognitive taxonomy use ki, jismein questions ki complexity ko L1 (information retrieval) se L4 (advanced system management) tak categorize kiya gaya. LLMs ko do tarah ke prompts ke saath test kiya gaya: ek simple baseline prompt aur ek detailed rubric-enhanced prompt. Ye tests 1200 real student responses par kiye gaye, jinhe pehle se hi teen expert instructors ne grade kiya tha.

Results ne dikhaya ki Gemini 3.0 Pro, jab use rubric-guided prompting ke saath use kiya gaya, toh usne human experts ke saath sabse accha agreement achieve kiya. Ek important finding yeh bhi thi ki jaise-jaise questions ki cognitive complexity badhti gayi (L1 se L4 ki taraf), LLMs ki grading accuracy kam hoti gayi. Overall, paper ne conclude kiya ki LLM provider se zyada, rubric ki quality aur structured prompts ka use grading agreement ko significantly improve karta hai. Is research ne ek framework provide kiya hai jisse decide kiya ja sakta hai ki kaun se questions AI-assisted grading ke liye suitable hain aur kaun se human review maangte hain.

Title: Automated grading of Linux/bash examinations using large language models: a four-level cognitive taxonomy approach 
Abstract: Scalable and reliable grading of command-line examinations remains a challenge in computing education, where rising enrolments make manual marking difficult and rule-based autograders cannot handle partial credit, equivalent solutions, or syntactic variation. This paper evaluates whether four frontier Large Language Models (GPT, Claude Opus, Gemini, and GLM) can approximate expert judgment when grading short Linux/bash command responses. The study adopts a four-level cognitive taxonomy that combines cognitive complexity and operational impact, ranging from information retrieval (L1) and basic file manipulation (L2) to structural operations (L3) and advanced system management (L4). The models were tested with two prompt variants, a minimal baseline and a rubric-enhanced version, on 1200 real responses from second-year Computer Engineering students independently graded by three expert instructors. Gemini~3.0 Pro with rubric-guided prompting achieved the highest human-AI agreement (ICC(3,1) = 0.888, MAE = 0.10, Bland-Altman bias = -0.014). Agreement declined consistently as taxonomy level increased, with the largest discrepancies at higher levels. Across all models, rubric quality had a larger effect than provider choice, with structured prompts consistently improving agreement. These results show that question complexity is a reliable predictor of the difficulty LLMs face in grading accurately, and they establish a principled, taxonomy-based framework for determining which questions are suitable for AI-assisted grading and which require human review, while also providing a transferable evaluation protocol and prompt templates.
output:
Is research paper se kuch important engineering aur algorithmic takeaways hain:

**1. Cognitive Taxonomy ka Role:** Paper ne ek four-level cognitive taxonomy introduce ki hai, jo questions ki complexity ko categorize karti hai. Yeh taxonomy sirf LLM performance ko evaluate karne ke liye hi nahi, balki AI-assisted grading ke liye questions ko filter out karne ke liye bhi ek structured framework provide karti hai. Matlab, hum pehle se hi identify kar sakte hain ki kaun se questions LLMs ke liye challenging honge.

**2. Prompt Engineering ki Criticality:** Results ne clearly dikhaya ki rubric quality ka impact LLM provider choice se zyada tha. Iska matlab hai ki LLMs ko effective aur detailed prompts (rubric-enhanced prompting) provide karna unki grading accuracy aur human expert agreement ko significantly improve karta hai. Yeh ek core principle hai ki LLM ki performance usko diye gaye instructions ki quality par bahut depend karti hai.

**3. Question Complexity as a Predictor:** Research ne establish kiya ki question complexity, jaisa ki taxonomy levels se define kiya gaya hai, LLMs ki grading difficulty ka ek reliable predictor hai. Higher cognitive levels par LLMs ki accuracy kam ho jaati hai. Is insight ko use karke hum AI-assisted grading systems ko design kar sakte hain jo lower-level questions ko automate karein aur higher-level questions ko human review ke liye flag karein.

**4. Transferable Evaluation Protocol:** Paper ne ek robust evaluation protocol aur prompt templates bhi provide kiye hain. Yeh dusre researchers aur educators ke liye ek valuable resource hai jo similar AI-assisted grading systems develop ya evaluate karna chahte hain, ensuring consistency aur reproducibility.

instruction: Explain the following AI research abstract in simple Hinglish.
input:
Title: WorldSample: Closed-loop Real-robot RL with World Modelling 
Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) can overcome the demonstration-coverage limitation of imitation learning (IL) by allowing robots to improve through trial-and-error interaction beyond the states observed in demonstrations. However, deploying RL on real robots remains constrained by high interaction costs, since each physical rollout is costly and reflects only one realized action-outcome path. To address this challenge, we propose WorldSample, a physically grounded data augmentation framework for real-robot RL that closes a real-synthetic loop between physical rollouts, world-model generation, and policy improvement. Grounded on real rollouts, WorldSample generates high-fidelity synthetic transitions through a post-trained world model, which greatly lowers the visual hallucination. Specifically, rather than simply using these transitions as real-world experience, WorldSample introduces Policy-Paced Learning (PPL) to regulate the training process through sample selection and scheduling, balancing useful augmentation against value overestimation and mitigating the hallucination-induced noise. Experiments on robot manipulation tasks involving contact-rich and precise tasks show that WorldSample improves policy success rate by 28% while reducing training steps by 59% compared with baselines. Furthermore, WorldSample improves world model visual fidelity by 19.4dB in PSNR and 0.47 in SSIM over demonstration-only post-training, validating the effectiveness of the real-synthetic loop for both policy and world model performance.
output:
Students, yeh paper 'WorldSample' ek bahut important problem solve kar raha hai real-robot Reinforcement Learning (RL) mein. Dekhiye, RL robots ko trial-and-error se seekhne deta hai, jo Imitation Learning (IL) ki ek limitation ko overcome karta hai jahan robot sirf pre-recorded demonstrations se seekhta hai. Lekin, real robots par RL deploy karna bahut costly hai. Kyunki har physical rollout, matlab robot ka har ek real-world interaction, bahut expensive hota hai aur usse sirf ek hi action-outcome path ka data milta hai.

Is challenge ko address karne ke liye, WorldSample ek naya framework propose karta hai. Yeh ek 'real-synthetic loop' banata hai. Iska matlab hai ki pehle robot kuch real physical rollouts karta hai. Phir, is real data ko use karke, ek 'world model' train kiya jaata hai. Yeh world model high-fidelity synthetic transitions generate karta hai, matlab virtual data jo real data jaisa hi hota hai aur visual hallucination ko kam karta hai. Is synthetic data ko simply real-world experience ki tarah use karne ke bajaye, WorldSample ek aur smart technique use karta hai jise Policy-Paced Learning (PPL) kehte hain. PPL ka kaam hai ki woh decide kare ki kaun sa synthetic data kab aur kaise policy training ke liye use kiya jaayega. Yeh useful augmentation aur value overestimation ya hallucination-induced noise ke beech balance banata hai. Isse robot ki policy ki performance improve hoti hai aur training steps bhi kam ho jaate hain. Overall, yeh real aur synthetic data ko smartly combine karke RL ko real robots ke liye zyada practical banata hai.

instruction: Explain the following AI research abstract in simple Hinglish.
input:
Title: Self-Auditing Residual Drifting for Pathology-Preserving Accelerated Knee MRI 
Abstract: Accelerated magnetic resonance imaging reduces acquisition time, but reconstruction from undersampled k-space can blur diagnostically relevant structures or introduce failures that are not captured by global image metrics. We propose SA-RDM-DC, a Self-Auditing Residual generative Drifting Model with Data Consistency for accelerated knee MRI. The method adapts the newly proposed generative drifting paradigm to accelerated MRI by training a physics-conditioned drift field from the zero-filled reconstruction toward the fully sampled residual correction. It predicts image- and missing-k-space residual corrections, enforces data consistency with acquired k-space, uses frequency-aware and residual drifting supervision to recover fine detail, and produces dense error maps and slice-level risk scores in the same inference pass. We evaluate SA-RDM-DC on multi-coil fastMRI knee data at acceleration factors of 4, 8, and 12, with fastMRI+ pathology annotations for region-level and classifier-based task preservation, and on SKM-TEA for zero-shot and fine-tuned protocol-shift evaluation. Compared with zero-filled reconstruction, UNet-image-SENSE, DC-UNet, Score-Diffusion, ELF-Diff, SENSE-VarNet, and MoDL baselines, SA-RDM-DC achieves the highest SSIM across fastMRI acceleration factors while retaining subsecond per-slice inference and avoiding the long sampling time of iterative diffusion baselines. In pathology-aware analysis, SA-RDM-DC preserves lesion-region structural fidelity and reduces meniscus prediction instability. Its self-auditing scores strongly identify high-error reconstructions on fastMRI and partially transfer as a selective-review signal under SKM-TEA protocol shift. These results support reconstruction evaluation that jointly considers image fidelity, pathology preservation, runtime, and case-specific reliability.
output:
Yeh paper accelerated MRI ke liye ek naya method, SA-RDM-DC, introduce karta hai. Accelerated MRI mein, scan time kam karne ke liye k-space data ko undersample kiya jaata hai. Lekin isse images blur ho sakti hain ya important diagnostic details miss ho sakte hain, jo standard image metrics se detect nahi hote.

SA-RDM-DC ek Self-Auditing Residual generative Drifting Model hai jisme Data Consistency bhi hai. Iska core idea yeh hai ki yeh ek 'drift field' train karta hai. Yeh drift field zero-filled reconstruction (jo undersampled data se banti hai) ko fully sampled residual correction ki taraf 'drift' karta hai. Matlab, yeh model original image aur missing k-space data ke liye corrections predict karta hai.

Yeh method acquired k-space data ke saath consistency maintain karta hai. Fine details recover karne ke liye, yeh frequency-aware aur residual drifting supervision use karta hai. Sabse khaas baat yeh hai ki yeh model inference ke time hi dense error maps aur slice-level risk scores bhi generate karta hai, jisse hume pata chalta hai ki kis image part mein kitni error ho sakti hai. Iski performance kaafi achhi hai, especially SSIM ke terms mein, aur yeh pathology details ko bhi preserve karta hai, jaise lesion-region structural fidelity aur meniscus prediction stability.

instruction: Explain the following AI research abstract in simple Hinglish.
input:
Title: QFedAgent: Quantum-Enhanced Personalized Federated Learning for Multi-Agent Activity Recognition 
Abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training across distributed devices without sharing raw data, making it suitable for privacy-sensitive robotic sensing applications. However, multi-agent systems generate heterogeneous and non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) multimodal sensor streams that degrade conventional FL algorithms, while classical fusion modules introduce substantial parameter overhead and communication cost. This paper proposes QFedAgent, a hybrid quantum-classical personalized FL framework for multi-agent activity recognition. The approach integrates a variational quantum circuit fusion module that models accelerometer--gyroscope interactions through quantum state encoding and entanglement, requiring only 72 quantum rotation parameters versus 33K in classical multi-layer perceptron-based fusion, achieving approximately 10x total parameter reduction. Experiments on the OPPORTUNITY dataset under subject-based non-IID partitions demonstrate 97.7% mean test accuracy, confirming that parameter-efficient quantum fusion remains competitive with conventional federated baselines.
output:
Yeh research paper QFedAgent ke baare mein hai, jo ek naya tareeka hai multi-agent systems mein activity recognition ke liye. Basically, yeh Federated Learning (FL) ko use karta hai, jismein multiple devices ya agents milkar ek common model train karte hain, lekin apna raw data share nahi karte. Isse data privacy maintain rehti hai, jo robotic sensing jaise applications ke liye bahut important hai.

Lekin, problem yeh hai ki multi-agent systems se jo data aata hai (jaise accelerometer aur gyroscope se), woh aksar heterogeneous aur non-IID (yani different agents ka data alag-alag pattern ka hota hai) hota hai. Isse traditional FL algorithms ki performance kharab ho jaati hai. Aur agar hum classical methods se in multimodal sensor streams ko fuse karte hain, toh usmein bahut zyada parameters aur communication cost lagta hai.

Is challenge ko address karne ke liye, QFedAgent ek hybrid quantum-classical personalized FL framework propose karta hai. Ismein ek special 'variational quantum circuit fusion module' use kiya gaya hai. Yeh module accelerometer aur gyroscope ke interactions ko quantum state encoding aur entanglement ke through model karta hai. Iska sabse bada benefit yeh hai ki ismein sirf 72 quantum rotation parameters lagte hain, jabki classical multi-layer perceptron-based fusion mein 33,000 parameters lagte the. Toh, isse approximately 10x total parameter reduction achieve hota hai.

Experiments OPPORTUNITY dataset par kiye gaye, jahan subject-based non-IID partitions use kiye gaye. Results mein 97.7% mean test accuracy mili, jo confirm karta hai ki yeh parameter-efficient quantum fusion classical federated baselines ke saath competitive hai.

instruction: Explain the following AI research abstract in simple Hinglish.
input:
Title: Learning to Evolve Scenes: Reasoning about Human Activities with Scene Graphs 
Abstract: Understanding human behavior while interacting with the surrounding world is crucial for many applications of embodied AI. First-person videos are particularly informative for this problem, as they well capture how activities reshape the scene over time. However, existing approaches often rely on implicit visual or language-aligned representations, disregarding structured reasoning over the scene dynamic. We argue that explicit, compositional and editable representations of human-environment interactions can play a crucial role for rich grounded activity understanding. To this end, we introduce SG-Ego, a large scale annotation set extending Ego4D with spatio-temporal scene graphs, where relations triplets are consolidated over time into explicit time-evolving descriptions of the scene state. To reason over this representation, we propose GLEN, a graph-based model that operates over scene graph sequences to both align them with textual actions and model their temporal evolution. In addition, we formulate the activity-driven graph-edit forecasting (A-GEF) problem, a novel task that casts scene dynamics as a sequence of structured transformations conditioned on ongoing actions, enabling explicit reasoning about how scenes change over time. We validate our approach across multiple downstream tasks, spanning retrieval benchmarks as EgoMCQ and EgoCVR, as well as long-horizon reasoning benchmarks as EXPLORE-Bench and the newly introduced A-GEF. GLEN achieves strong results compared to raw video baselines and it excels in reasoning settings, typically addressed only with MLLMs, while enabling controllable and structured predictions of scene dynamics driven by human activities. We believe our results establish spatio-temporal scene graphs, together with models that reason over them, as strong compositional and interpretable representations for video understanding and potentially beyond.

Yeh research paper human activities ko understand karne ke liye ek naya approach propose karta hai, khaaskar first-person videos se. Current methods aksar implicit representations use karte hain, jisse scene mein hone wale changes ko structured tareeke se samajhna mushkil hota hai.

Paper ka main idea hai explicit, compositional, aur editable representations use karna, jinko spatio-temporal scene graphs kehte hain. Yeh scene graphs objects, unke attributes, aur unke beech ke relationships ko time ke saath kaise evolve karte hain, yeh explicitly describe karte hain. Iske liye, inhone SG-Ego naam ka ek large-scale annotation set banaya hai, jo Ego4D dataset ko spatio-temporal scene graphs se extend karta hai.

Is naye representation par reasoning karne ke liye, inhone GLEN naam ka ek graph-based model introduce kiya hai. GLEN scene graph sequences par operate karta hai, unhe textual actions ke saath align karta hai aur unke temporal evolution ko model karta hai. Matlab, yeh model bata sakta hai ki scene mein kya ho raha hai aur future mein kya ho sakta hai, human actions ke basis par.

Ek aur important contribution hai activity-driven graph-edit forecasting (A-GEF) problem. Yeh ek naya task hai jisme scene dynamics ko structured transformations ki sequence ke roop mein dekha jaata hai, jo ongoing actions par conditioned hoti hain.
